verdict_reason: Every measured number in README.md and data/ was reproduced exactly by independent code (exhaustive k = 16 census of 2,141,033,203 pairs, seed-rule replays of all four sampled cells, curve facts by two methods, the discriminant identity symbolically, P5/P6 and point arithmetic). Main result reproduced: 0 of 1,070,453,835 mixed pairs at k = 16 have an F_p root. Errata are scope and labelling: P6's wording versus the x = 0 diagonal pair, the given-cell flag label, untagged or unlabelled derived sentences (factor-base implication), attribution, timing label and reproducibility logging. No erratum changes a count or the P1 conclusion.
independence: Validator code in the session scratchpad (vcore.py, v_facts.py, v_identity.py, v_exhaustive.py, v_p5p6_points.py, v_replay.py, v_compare.py) imports none of l4core.py, run_l4.py, controls.py, analyze_l4.py; only the protocol text (seed rule, polynomial) was reused. analyze_l4.py was run once, on a scratch copy, solely to check that results_main.{md,json} regenerate from the JSONs.

checks.detail: Euler-criterion character sums give #E = 65672, 1049624, 16784072 and twist orders 65204, 1047524, 16770212 for k = 16, 20, 24; x-only ladder point orders on random E-class and T-class x have lcm equal to these orders and each is the unique multiple of the lcm in the Hasse interval (E(F_p) cyclic of order 8r, twist cyclic of order 4r'). r = 8209, 131203, 2098009 and r' = 16301, 261881, 4192553 are prime (trial division); #E + #twist = 2p + 2; A^2 - 4 non-square at every k so Z = {0}; x-class counts Z/E/T = 1/32835/32601, 1/524811/523761, 1/8392035/8385105. checks.name: (2) discriminant identity disc/4 = 4 f(x1) f(x2), symbolic
checks.detail: Expanded B2^2 - (x1-x2)^2 (x1 x2-1)^2 - 4 f(x1) f(x2) in Z[x1, x2, A] with the validator's own polynomial arithmetic: the zero polynomial. The identity therefore holds over every F_p (not only on sampled pairs), and the reversed ('given') polynomial has the same disc/4 because a c is symmetric.

checks.name: (2) consequence: mixed pairs have no F_p root (brute force, no discriminant used)
checks.detail: At p = 101 and p = 103, for every A with A^2 != 4 (99 and 101 values, about half with full rational 2-torsion), S3 was evaluated at every X in F_p for every pair: mixed (E,T) pairs with an F_p root 0 of 480300 and 0 of 510102; non-diagonal non-Z same-class pairs with != 2 roots 0; same-class roots on the other curve 0; identity failures 0. Derivation: with a = (x1-x2)^2 != 0 (mixed implies x1 != x2), disc/4 = 4 f(x1) f(x2) is (square)(non-square), a non-square, so no F_p root.

checks.name: (4) P5 2-torsion-translate counts
checks.detail: S3(x1, x2, 0) = (x1 x2 - 1)^2, so a root at x = 0 (the only Z point) occurs iff x1 x2 = 1; x(P + T0) = 1/x confirmed by explicit addition on 4000 points per k; f(1/x) = f(x)/x^4 for every x != 0 so the class is preserved. Unordered pairs {x, 1/x}, x != 1/x: k16 EE 16417, TT 16300, ET 0; k20 262405, 261880; k24 4196017, 4192552 (= (|class| - 1)/2; x = 1 and x = -1 are the 2 fixed points). The validator's exhaustive census has exactly 16417 (E,E) and 16300 (twist,twist) non-diagonal pairs with a root at x = 0, 0 mixed: equal to 16417 and 16300. Sampled k20: observed 390, 420 vs expected 381.09, 381.85 (z = 0.46, 1.95); k24: 4, 2 vs 5.96, 5.96 (z = -0.80, -1.62), recomputed from unrounded values.

checks.name: (4) P6 diagonal
checks.detail: For every non-Z x the linear S3 root c/(2 B2) equals x(2P) from the Weierstrass doubling formula, and lies on the point's own curve except x = 1 and x = -1 (x(2P) = 0) at every k; 0 on the other curve. The single ZZ diagonal pair x1 = x2 = 0 has B2 = 0, c = 1: no finite root (2 T0 = O). The frozen P6 wording ('x1 = x2: exactly one finite root x(2P) ... 100%') does not cover it, and analyze_l4.py evaluates P6 on EE/TT diagonals only. See erratum E1.

checks.name: (5) (E,E) and (T,T) roots equal x(P1 +- P2) by the validator's point arithmetic
checks.detail: Long-Weierstrass affine addition (twist mapped to Y^2 = X^3 + A n X^2 + n^2 X, X = n x, with a large non-residue n, not the producer's smallest one): k16 EE 19999/19999, TT 19999/19999; k20 20000/20000, 20000/20000; k24 5000/5000, 5000/5000 root sets equal; S3 vanishes at both sums in every case. Mixed pairs over F_p^2 (2000 per k): both x(P1 +- P2) are S3 roots, conjugate, outside F_p; 300 k16 mixed pairs evaluated at all 65437 X: 0 roots.

errata.text: P6 as frozen ('x1 = x2: exactly one finite root x(2P) ... 100%') does not hold for the one ZZ diagonal pair x1 = x2 = 0: 2 T0 = O, S3 degenerates to the constant 1 and has no finite root (README exhaustive table row '(Z,Z) yes 1 pair, 0 roots'; same in the k = 20 and k = 24 Z strata, omitted from the README sampled table). analyze_l4.py evaluates P6 on the EE and TT diagonals only, so 'P6 held' and 'All 10 numbered predictions (P1 to P10) held; none failed' overstate the frozen wording. The exception follows from the mathematics and the count is otherwise exact (32,835 E and 32,601 twist diagonal pairs).
errata.suggested_fix: In the README Errata section (or a sibling ERRATA.md; leave data/ byte-equal): state that P6 as worded fails on 1 of 65,437 diagonal pairs at k = 16 (x = 0, 2 T0 = O, 0 finite roots), that P6 held on the EE/TT diagonals, and replace 'none failed' with '9 held as worded; P6 held on the EE/TT diagonals and fails on the x = 0 diagonal pair, which the protocol did not except'.

errata.text: In data/results_main.md the 'given' cells label the leading-coefficient-zero flag as 'x1=x2'. For the given polynomial a = (x1 x2 - 1)^2, so the flag marks x1 x2 = 1 pairs (the ZZ pair (0,0) appears as 'x1=x2 False'). Validator replay: k = 16 given has 1595 (E,E) and 1594 (twist,twist) pairs with x1 x2 = 1 but 1474 and 1518 with x1 = x2; k = 20 given 94/99 vs 91/97. The P6 lines of the given cells therefore test x1 x2 = 1 pairs, and README's '100% two-root same-class pairs' for the given cells holds only for pairs with x1 x2 != 1 (those have one finite root, the other at infinity).
errata.suggested_fix: Errata note: the column is 'a = 0 (x1 x2 = 1)' in the given cells, the given-cell P6 lines are about x1 x2 = 1 pairs, and the README sentence becomes '100% two-root same-class pairs with x1 x2 != 1; the 1595 + 1594 (k = 16) and 94 + 99 (k = 20) pairs with x1 x2 = 1 have one finite root'.

errata.text: The factor-base implication is not consistently labelled derived and is mostly untagged: 'What the outcome implies for twist points in a factor base' states 'Twist points therefore add no relations for a target on E', 'They serve only the twist's own discrete logarithm ... which carries no information about E', 'The only mixed rational relations run through translation by 2-torsion (P5) ... as in the torsion leads' and 'A factor base using twist x-coordinates lowers the density of usable columns' as facts without [pcc:unverified] or a derived label; Answer item 4's first sentence is also untagged; 'Derived versus measured' omits the implication (PROTOCOL section 7 calls it 'a derivation plus count'). 'As in the torsion leads' cites a study that 'Sources checked' says was not read. 'Can use only E-class base points' omits x = 0 (T0), which does give relations S3(x_Q, 0, 1/x_Q) = 0.
errata.suggested_fix: Add a 'Derived (argued from the S3 counts, not measured): factor-base implication' bullet to 'Derived versus measured', tag each sentence of the implication section, drop or source 'as in the torsion leads', and write 'only E-class base points or x = 0'.

errata.text: Other result sentences without [pcc:unverified]: 'At every k the only rational 2-torsion x is 0 (A^2 - 4 is a non-square).'; 'Positive controls (P7a, P7b) show the counter and the mechanism are visible.'; the bold lead sentences of Answer items 1-3 (the following sentences are tagged).

README heading 'Erratum to the brief' says 'The brief writes S3 = (x1 x2 - 1)^2 x3^2 ...', but research/curve25519_wave7_untried_20261122/BRIEF.md contains no S3 formula; PROTOCOL section 2 correctly attributes the reversed form to 'the task text'.
errata.suggested_fix: Retitle to 'Erratum to the task text' and replace 'the brief' by 'the L4 task text (dispatch)' in that section.

errata.text: Times labelled 'CPU' (305 s, 97 s, 52 s; cpu_seconds in the JSONs) are wall-clock time.time() intervals on a loaded shared host, not CPU time.
errata.suggested_fix: Relabel as 'wall s (shared host)'; use time.process_time() in future runs.

errata.text: Reproducibility binding is incomplete: run.log does not echo the commands (only the launch commit and outputs, consistent with run_all.sh), and neither run.log nor the run JSONs record the git commit, python or numpy version (the validator's replay on this host, numpy 2.5.3, reproduced every sampled draw, so the binding holds here de facto). results_main.md prints 'complete=True' for sampled cells from d.get('complete', True), a default rather than a recorded field (harmless: it only gates exhaustive-mode P5).
errata.suggested_fix: Errata note recording python 3.13.18 / numpy 2.5.3 as the replay environment; future launchers log 'set -x' command lines and write commit and versions into each JSON.

errata.text: P10 has no machine verdict: analyze_l4.py evaluates P1-P9 only, and the code never tests r or r' for primality (it follows from complete trial division in factor_small). README's 'P10 held' is read off the curve-facts line. The validator confirms P10 independently.
errata.suggested_fix: Say 'P10 held (read from curve_facts; confirmed by the validator)'.

errata.text: The README sampled table puts 'roots on twist' before 'roots on E', the reverse of the exhaustive table, and omits the diagonal and ZZ rows (370/387 and 3/3 diagonal pairs, 1 ZZ pair) that are included in its pair totals. Values are correct.
